Let's not forget that food is a huge part of culture, and a country's cultural image is shaped by its economic strength and international relationships. Japan is an interesting example. Think about how it became the West's closest Asian allies after WWII, particularly with the US, and how much Japanese culture has since been promoted and embraced in the West.
I see this in Australia and NZ as well. I have chef friends who love Chinese food, but for years none of them would even think about travelling to China let alone to go there learn the cuisine. I don't think that was really about the food, it’s more about how China itself was perceived. Fortunately that's started changing recently, partly because social media is showing people a very different side of China. Chongqing's whole cyberpunk trend is an example.
